about: Oracle Customer Orders workload for tools/sample_db_bench.py. origin 'upstream-view': the four views upstream ships (customer_order_products, store_orders, product_reviews, product_orders in co_create.sql, at the pinned commit), adapted to BigQuery as 'adaptation' says; 'authored': written for this eval.

queries.name: customer_order_products
queries.adaptation: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS dropped; LISTAGG(p.product_name, ', ' ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE '...' WITH COUNT) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY oi.line_item_id) becomes STRING_AGG(p.product_name, ', ' ORDER BY oi.line_item_id) (no overflow truncation: no list is near Oracle's 4000-byte limit); column aliases written with AS
queries.sql: SELECT o.order_id, o.order_tms, o.order_status, c.customer_id, c.email_address, c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS order_total, STRING_AGG(p.product_name, ', ' ORDER BY oi.line_item_id) AS items FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.order_tms, o.order_status, c.customer_id, c.email_address, c.full_name

queries.name: store_orders
queries.adaptation: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS dropped; GROUPING_ID(store_name, order_status) becomes GROUPING(s.store_name) * 2 + GROUPING(o.order_status) (the same bit vector; BigQuery has GROUPING, not GROUPING_ID); column aliases written with AS
queries.sql: SELECT CASE GROUPING(s.store_name) * 2 + GROUPING(o.order_status) WHEN 1 THEN 'STORE TOTAL' WHEN 2 THEN 'STATUS TOTAL' WHEN 3 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' END AS total, s.store_name, COALESCE(s.web_address, s.physical_address) AS address, s.latitude, s.longitude, o.order_status, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales FROM stores AS s JOIN orders AS o ON s.store_id = o.store_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((s.store_name, COALESCE(s.web_address, s.physical_address), s.latitude, s.longitude), (s.store_name, COALESCE(s.web_address, s.physical_address), s.latitude, s.longitude, o.order_status), o.order_status, ())

queries.name: product_reviews
queries.adaptation: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS dropped; JSON_TABLE(p.product_details, '$' COLUMNS (NESTED PATH '$.reviews[*]' COLUMNS (rating INTEGER PATH '$.rating', review VARCHAR2(4000) PATH '$.review'))) becomes a LEFT JOIN UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(PARSE_JSON(product_details), '$.reviews')) with JSON_VALUE for the two fields (a nested path keeps a product with no reviews, as the LEFT JOIN does); the window AVG over the product name needs the extracted rating, so it sits in an outer query
queries.sql: SELECT product_name, rating, ROUND(AVG(rating) OVER (PARTITION BY product_name), 2) AS avg_rating, review FROM (SELECT p.product_name, CAST(JSON_VALUE(r, '$.rating') AS INT64) AS rating, JSON_VALUE(r, '$.review') AS review FROM products AS p LEFT JOIN UNNEST(JSON_QUERY_ARRAY(PARSE_JSON(p.product_details), '$.reviews')) AS r) AS reviews

queries.name: product_orders
queries.adaptation: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW ... AS dropped; column aliases written with AS
queries.sql: SELECT p.product_name, o.order_status, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_sales, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name, o.order_status
SELECT o.order_id, o.order_status, c.full_name FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, s.shipment_status FROM order_items AS oi LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON oi.shipment_id = s.shipment_id

SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS spend FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 500
SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM orders
SELECT DISTINCT order_id, line_item_id, product_id FROM order_items
SELECT customer_id, full_name FROM customers WHERE customer_id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'REFUNDED')
SELECT o.order_id FROM orders AS o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items AS oi WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND oi.shipment_id IS NULL)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.full_name FROM customers AS c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'REFUNDED')
SELECT shipment_id FROM shipments WHERE shipment_id NOT IN (SELECT shipment_id FROM order_items)
SELECT product_id, product_name FROM products WHERE product_id NOT IN (SELECT product_id FROM inventory WHERE store_id = 5)
SELECT product_id, product_name, unit_price FROM products WHERE unit_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM products)

SELECT t.order_id, t.customer_id, t.total FROM (SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id) AS t WHERE t.total > (SELECT AVG(oi2.quantity * oi2.unit_price) FROM orders AS o2 JOIN order_items AS oi2 ON oi2.order_id = o2.order_id WHERE o2.customer_id = t.customer_id)
SELECT order_status AS status FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT shipment_status AS status FROM shipments
SELECT order_status AS status FROM orders UNION DISTINCT SELECT shipment_status AS status FROM shipments
SELECT customer_id FROM orders INTERSECT DISTINCT SELECT customer_id FROM shipments
SELECT customer_id FROM customers EXCEPT DISTINCT SELECT customer_id FROM shipments
SELECT product_id, revenue, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank FROM (SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id) AS r
SELECT order_id, order_tms, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY order_tms, order_id) AS orders_so_far FROM orders
SELECT order_id, customer_id, order_tms, LAG(order_tms) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_tms, order_id) AS previous_order FROM orders

WITH complete AS (SELECT order_id, store_id FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'COMPLETE'), unused AS (SELECT product_id FROM products), per_store AS (SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM complete GROUP BY store_id) SELECT s.store_name, p.n FROM per_store AS p JOIN stores AS s ON s.store_id = p.store_id
SELECT t.order_id, t.customer_id FROM (SELECT order_id, customer_id, store_id FROM orders WHERE 1 = 1 AND TRUE) AS t WHERE t.store_id = 1
SELECT ((oi.order_id)), (oi.quantity * (oi.unit_price)) AS line_total FROM order_items AS oi WHERE ((oi.quantity > 2)) AND (oi.unit_price < (50))
SELECT s.store_name, SUM(i.product_inventory) AS units FROM stores AS s LEFT JOIN inventory AS i ON i.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name
SELECT JSON_VALUE(PARSE_JSON(product_details), '$.colour') AS colour, COUNT(*) AS products FROM products GROUP BY colour
SELECT DATE_TRUNC(DATE(order_tms), MONTH) AS month, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY month
SELECT oi.order_id, oi.line_item_id, oi.unit_price, p.unit_price AS list_price FROM order_items AS oi JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE oi.unit_price <> p.unit_price
SELECT oi.order_id, oi.product_id FROM order_items AS oi JOIN orders AS o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id

SELECT a.product_id AS first_product, b.product_id AS second_product, COUNT(*) AS together FROM order_items AS a JOIN order_items AS b ON a.order_id = b.order_id AND a.product_id < b.product_id GROUP BY a.product_id, b.product_id
SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(s.shipment_id) AS shipments FROM customers AS c LEFT JOIN shipments AS s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id
SELECT o.order_id, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units FROM orders AS o JOIN order_items AS oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY o.order_id ORDER BY units DESC, o.order_id LIMIT 10
